blocks.text: Let's solve this one step by step. Tickets cost twelve dollars each and popcorn costs six. A three dollar coupon is taken off. Write an expression for the cost of x tickets and one popcorn.
blocks.display: Tickets cost 12 dollars each and popcorn costs 6. A 3 dollar coupon is taken off. Write an expression for the cost of x tickets and one popcorn.

blocks.text: Tickets cost twelve each, so x tickets cost twelve x.
Now combine the constants: six minus three is three, so twelve x plus three.
So the answer is twelve x plus three. Test it. If x is five, the expression gives sixty-three.
Watch out for these traps. If you add the coupon, you get twelve x plus nine. If you multiply the popcorn by twelve too, you get twelve times the quantity x plus six, minus three.
